profile.campus: Google Northern Virginia (Reston / Loudoun County / Prince William County), VA
profile.address: Energy Park Drive, Sycolin, Goose Creek Village, Loudoun County, VA 20147 (Stonewall Creek Business Park, Leesburg)
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Northern Virginia data center footprint, mapped near Leesburg at the Stonewall Creek Business Park along Energy Park Drive in the Sycolin/Goose Creek Village area of Loudoun County. Google's own Virginia locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within its Northern Virginia footprint, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived business-park name and street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Virginia data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company established a Virginia presence in 2009, purchased Northern Virginia land in 2017, opened its first facility in 2019, expanded a second Loudoun County facility in 2021, and opened a third in Prince William County in 2023; in 2025 Google announced a $9 billion investment for 2025-2026 spanning existing Northern Virginia sites and a new Chesterfield County campus. Google reports $15.6 billion in Virginia economic activity and over 36,000 employee volunteer hours since 2010.

Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley corridor, of which this Leesburg-area building is part, hosts large single-tenant campuses for AWS and Meta and colocation operators including Digital Realty and Equinix, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Virginia footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings or per-building capacity figures.

Loudoun and Prince William counties sit at the center of what industry trackers call Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world by aggregate power draw, a status Loudoun County's own economic development office has cited in public materials for over a decade. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has repeatedly flagged this corridor in integrated resource plan filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory, prompting new transmission and generation investment. Virginia's data center sales-and-use tax exemption, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership and renewed by the General Assembly, has been a material factor in Google and other hyperscalers continuing to expand in the corridor rather than building only in lower-tax states, though Google has not disclosed how much exemption value this specific facility has claimed.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus at Stonewall Creek Business Park in Loudoun County, Virginia, part of a multi-site expansion announced in April 2024 with $1 billion in planned investment across Loudoun and Prince William Counties. The company does not publish power capacity, square footage, or facility-specific megawatt figures for individual buildings, disclosing only aggregate investment and state-level data. The specific power draw of this location is not available.

Without published capacity figures, the campus cannot be ranked within Virginia's mapped facilities or compared to the 1,375 MW of published data center load across the state's 23 facilities with disclosed specifications. The site is one of 326 mapped data center locations in Virginia, but its contribution to state capacity remains opaque.

Google's disclosure policy makes it impossible to assess whether this campus matters to AI scaling in the state or to determine its position in the grid's binding constraints on compute. The operator's decision to withhold facility-level specifications limits visibility into the infrastructure supporting its regional AI operations.
